transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll is out with insights into how likely voters are viewing the midterm election.
President Trump continues to be unpopular with an approval rating among likely voters at 40 percent.
NPR's Domenico Montanaro says this generally puts Democrats in a strong position heading into election night, but that's only part of the story.
Everyone would rightly be shocked if Democrats don't win the House at this point.
You know, the polling error would have to be bigger than almost anything we've ever seen before.
But there could be limits to how big those gains are that Democrats would make.
And the Senate is genuinely a toss-up.
When we look at the targeted seats in the House, 9 in 10 are in districts that Trump won.
NPR's Domenico Montanaro reporting.
Israeli voters are deciding whether to re-elect Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Today's election is the first since the 2023 Hamas-led attack on Israel that ignited the war in Gaza and other regional conflicts.
Some Palestinian prisoners say they are hoping the results of the Israeli elections will lead to the ouster of Israel's far-right national security minister.
Itamar Vengar, NPR's Anis Baba, has more.
Vengavir has made restricting Palestinians prisoners food and access to showers a hallmark of his tenure.
He once said he drove several hours to a prison to investigate why a detainee had been given two extra olives.
His re-election videos have shown him touting Palestinian prisoners when word spread at Lavi present that Vengavir could lose his position.
Eight prisoners began saving slices of bread, corn, spoonfuls of jam, and tomatoes to assemble a layered cake.
Vengavir says the men saved a slice of bread here, another slice of bread there, to make it.
He says they were placed in solitary confinement after the cake was discovered.
Anis Baba, NPR News, Gaza.
Another top official at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is leaving the agency.
NPR's Rob Stein has that story.
Dr. Jennifer Shuford is stepping down as the CDC's chief medical officer and deputy director after six months on the job.
Shuford says she's leaving to spend more time with her family.
The departure is just the latest upheaval at the nation's premier public health agency, which has been rocked by mass firings, budget cuts, leadership turmoil, and charges of political interference by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
All this comes as the CDC has been largely silent on the role of vaccination in fighting the worst U.S. measles outbreak in decades.
Rob Stein, NPR News.
From Washington, this is NPR News.
Polls show cost of living remains top of mind among voters heading into the midterms, but today the conference board is reporting higher consumer confidence this month as gas prices eased.
The nonpartisan business membership and research group says its reading rose to 91.7 from 84.2 last month.
The Ukrainian T-shaped radio telescope Model 2 observes very low-frequency radio waves.
But as reporter Ari Daniel explains, it's been heavily damaged during the war with Russia.
Russian forces occupied the observatory outside of Kharkiv, where the telescope is based, at the start of the war, says radio astronomer Vyacheslav Zakharenko.
Practically all this building was usually damaged.
It's not safe for researchers to return to work, but they're planning a massive upgrade of the telescope, using what's happened as an opportunity to modernize the entire system.
We don't need to wait for end of war. We start now.
They can't do any installation until hostilities cease, but they can spec things out and build the components.
The updated telescope will be able to observe a greater range of radio waves and peer at different parts of the sky simultaneously.
For NPR News, I'm Ari Daniel.
An anonymous bidder is the new owner of a distant cousin of the T-Rex.
The auction house Sotheby says the fossil of the Nanotyrannus, nicknamed Jodi, has sold for $47.3 million.
That's far more than the $6 to $9 million it was expected to fetch.
This is NPR News.
You can now sponsor free through Amazon Music.
Or you can also support NPR's vital journalism and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.

topics.text: NPR/PBS/Marist poll shows Trump at 40% approval and Democrats favored in midterms
Israeli voters head to polls to decide whether to re-elect Netanyahu
Israeli minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's treatment of Palestinian prisoners draws scrutiny ahead of election
CDC chief medical officer Jennifer Shuford steps down after six months
Conference Board reports consumer confidence rose to 91.7 as gas prices eased
Ukraine's T-shaped radio telescope damaged during war with Russia faces planned upgrade
Nanotyrannus fossil nicknamed Jodi sells at auction for $47.3 million
